body:
Source: GitHub issues #1035 (security, P2) and #1036 (security, P2), both residuals of the #1019 review (PR #1029), deferred there because each needed a design decision. Both decisions are now made (see NORMATIVE). ONE ticket because both edit `lib/io.mjs` and the `--apply` branch of the bin; splitting them would have each rail the other's files.

Re-verified on main @ 076957c3.

**#1035 — the gate ledger is unsigned local state.** `.adlc/backlog-groom-ledger.json` is the ONLY source of authorization on the apply path (`lib/execute.mjs` `planAction` refuses anything the ledger does not approve, precisely so a caller-supplied `gate` field cannot authorize itself). But `ledgerApproves` (`lib/gate.mjs:76`) checks only fields the caller can compute: `verdict`, `contentHash`, `number`, `action`, `field`, `artifactDigest` — and `artifactDigest(action)` is an exported pure function of the action. Writing one JSON object into the ledger gets an issue commented and closed with zero reviews.

**#1036 — the floor's baseline comes from local refs.** `resolveTrustedBaseRef` (`lib/io.mjs:88`) reads `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, falling back to the literal `origin/main`, then `baseProfileFromGit` takes `git merge-base HEAD <ref>`. Those are ordinary local refs: `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main HEAD` makes the merge base the working commit, so a locally committed widened `autonomyFloor` (or narrowed `frozenPaths`) compares equal to itself and is accepted — the exact hole the removal of `--base-ref` was meant to close, reached through git instead of a flag. The package's own e2e fixture does this `update-ref` to build its base, which shows how available the move is.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/backlog-groom`: `bin/backlog-groom.mjs` (the `--apply` branch wires everything), `lib/apply.mjs` (`applyRun`, `revalidateAction`), `lib/execute.mjs` (`executeActions`, `planAction`), `lib/gate.mjs` (`gateAction`, `gateKey`, `artifactDigest`, `ledgerApproves`, `makeReviewRunner`), `lib/io.mjs` (`loadLedger`, `saveLedger`, `acquireApplyLock`, `resolveTrustedBaseRef`, `baseProfileFromGit`), `lib/floor.mjs` (`assertFloor`, `assertFloorNotWidened`, `assertFrozenPathsNotNarrowed`). Tests: `npm test -w packages/backlog-groom` (434 today). Spawned-binary tests live in `test/apply-e2e.test.mjs`; its `sandbox()` helper builds a temp git repo with a fake `gh` on PATH — extend it rather than inventing a second harness, and note its fake `gh` must keep draining stdin.

A null/unreadable base ALREADY fails closed: `lib/floor.mjs:116-120` and `:148` refuse rather than assume a floor. So every new failure path here should resolve to "no base", not to a permissive default.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.

1. **Ledger entries are HMAC-signed, and an unsigned or invalid entry is not an approval.** New `lib/ledger-sig.mjs` exporting `signLedgerEntry(key, entry)` and `verifyLedgerEntry(key, entry)`: HMAC-SHA256 over `LEDGER_SIG_DOMAIN + canonicalJson(entry-without-sig)`, compared with `timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, returning false (never throwing) for a missing, malformed or wrong `sig`. `LEDGER_SIG_DOMAIN` is a distinct constant (e.g. `adlc:backlog-groom-ledger:v1`) so ledger bytes can never collide with another artifact's signature.
2. **Do NOT import `@adlc/gate-manifest`'s `sign.mjs` for this.** Its `exports` map is root-only (`"exports": "./index.mjs"`, which re-exports only `appendManifestEntry`), so reaching `lib/sign.mjs` would mean widening an ENFORCEMENT_PREFIXES package's public surface — making every future ledger change a trust-root change. The local implementation is a few lines of `node:crypto`; say so at its definition.
3. **The key is `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY`, read from the environment in the bin only** and threaded down. With NO key: nothing can be signed or verified, so every action demotes to a proposal and the run still produces its report and exits 0, printing one clear line to stderr saying that writes are disabled because no key is present. This is the designed posture — proposing is unattended, closing is a key-holder act — not a failure to work around.
4. **Every write to a ledger entry re-signs it, and every read that grants anything verifies it.** `ledgerApproves` requires a valid signature in addition to its existing field checks. The `applied === true` short-circuit in `executeActions` also requires a valid signature, because a forged `applied` makes the tool report an action as executed while writing nothing.
5. **Existing unsigned ledger entries are not approvals.** There is no migration and no legacy tolerance: an old entry re-reviews rather than executing. A `--force`-style override does not exist.
6. **The floor baseline is anchored to the REMOTE.** Replace the local-ref resolution: derive `owner/repo` from `git remote get-url origin`, ask the forge for the default branch (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}`), resolve that branch's head on the remote (`git ls-remote origin <branch>`), and use `git merge-base HEAD <remoteSha>` as the baseline commit. The resulting base must be an ancestor of that remote head (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), so a moved local ref cannot decide it.
7. **Every failure of step 6 refuses.** No origin remote, gh unavailable or erroring, `ls-remote` failing, an empty or malformed sha, or a merge base that is not an ancestor of the remote head all resolve to "no base", which the existing floor guards already turn into a refusal. Never fall back to a local ref, and never assume the default profile on a resolution failure.
8. **The read path is unchanged.** `--apply` already requires `gh` and the network; a plain groom run must not gain a remote call, and its offline behaviour must stay exactly as it is.
9. Documentation: `packages/backlog-groom/README.md` plus the hand-maintained mirrors `docs/tools/backlog-groom.md` and `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/backlog-groom.mdx`, and `.claude/skills/backlog-groom/SKILL.md`. The existing text that says the ledger is not a trust boundary, and that the autonomy floor rather than the ledger is what stands between a groomed set and a closed issue, is now WRONG and must be corrected rather than left beside the new behaviour.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 A hand-written ledger entry with no `sig` grants nothing: the action demotes, and nothing is written to GitHub. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/ledger-signature.test.mjs`
- AC2 An entry whose content is edited after signing (any signed field, including `verdict`, `artifactDigest` or `number`) fails verification and grants nothing. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/ledger-signature.test.mjs`
- AC3 A correctly signed approval still executes exactly as before — comment first, then the action. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/apply-e2e.test.mjs`
- AC4 A forged `applied: true` does not short-circuit: the run does not report the action as executed. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/ledger-signature.test.mjs`
- AC5 With no `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY`, `--apply` exits 0, writes nothing, reports the actions as demoted, and says on stderr that writes are disabled for want of a key. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/apply-e2e.test.mjs`
- AC6 `verifyLedgerEntry` is constant-time on equal-length input and returns false (never throws) for missing, malformed, wrong-length and wrong-value signatures. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/ledger-signature.test.mjs`
- AC7 Moving a local ref no longer moves the baseline: with `refs/remotes/origin/main` pointed at HEAD and a locally committed widened floor, `--apply` refuses instead of accepting. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/remote-base.test.mjs`
- AC8 Each remote-resolution failure (no origin, gh error, ls-remote failure, non-ancestor merge base) refuses rather than falling back. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/remote-base.test.mjs`
- AC9 The read path issues no remote call and still works offline. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/remote-base.test.mjs`
- AC10 Existing suite green. verify: `npm test -w packages/backlog-groom`
- AC11 Docs corrected in all four places, including the now-false "ledger is not a trust boundary" text. verify: `grep -rn "not a trust boundary" packages/backlog-groom/README.md docs/tools/backlog-groom.md apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/backlog-groom.mdx` shows no claim that the LEDGER is unauthenticated
- AC12 Mutation gate green. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally)

OUT OF SCOPE: #1037 (`GH_REPO` retargeting writes) — same family, separate issue, and its fix is to bind the gh target to the checkout's origin rather than to authorize anything; widening `@adlc/gate-manifest`'s exports so its signing helpers can be shared (would make this a trust-root change); any change to the review cadence or the one-shot rule; the relation threshold.
title: backlog-groom: make the write path's two authorization inputs unforgeable — sign the ledger, anchor the floor baseline to the remote
